paragraphs: Getting a substrate positioned exactly right, every time, is what separates a systematic study from a series of one-off coating attempts.

The high-flatness, aluminum sample holder gives flexible and rigid substrates up to 300 × 200 mm a consistent, reliable surface to sit on, removing substrate flatness as a variable in your results. The infinite-step height and lateral position manual dial then lets you fine-tune positioning with full control, supporting quick-reaction experimental runs as well as longer, more systematic studies, all without handing that control over to automation.

sections.title: Stepping Up From Spin Coating
sections.tabSummary: Why scalarSC is the natural next step
body: Why FOM scalarSC is positioned as the natural next step from spin coating.
Spin coating gets you a film. It doesn't tell you whether that film's formation process will translate to anything industry-relevant, and that's the gap FOM scalarSC is built to close.

Whether your work is fundamental research or new product development, FOM scalarSC serves as the step from spin coating toward medium-scale, industry-relevant processing, on rigid or flexible substrates as your work requires. Its compact setup installs easily inside a laminar flow hood or glove box, and the external syringe pump keeps that workspace design flexible rather than constrained by integrated pump hardware.

paragraphs: Sample flatness sounds like a small detail until it distorts an entire coating run, and most sheet coaters solve it with extra manual steps to fixate the substrate in place.

FOM vectorSC's proprietary substrate holder takes a different approach, using a microporous structure that provides homogeneous suction across the substrate itself. That suction holds the sample flat directly, without needing the extra fixation steps typically required elsewhere, saving time on every single run rather than just occasionally. The result is excellent substrate flatness as a built-in property of the system, not something the operator has to work to achieve each time.
sections.note: Tell us your typical substrate material and thickness, and we'll confirm how the microporous holder performs with your samples.
sections.tabSummary: How homogeneous suction achieves excellent flatness

sections.title: Integrated Pump and Remote Operation
sections.tabSummary: What cloud-based control actually enables
body: What FOM vectorSC's built-in pump and cloud-based software actually enable.
Precursor delivery and remote access are usually two separate problems. FOM vectorSC solves them together by building the pump directly into the tool and pairing it with cloud-based control.

Because the pump is integrated rather than external, precursor delivery becomes part of the same controlled system as substrate positioning and coating parameters, rather than a separate piece of hardware to manage alongside it. Cloud-based software then extends that control beyond the physical lab, enabling genuine remote operation and diagnostics, useful for teams checking in on a run from elsewhere, or for troubleshooting support without needing someone physically present at the machine.

longForm.heroHook: Save a coating protocol once. Call it back and reproduce it exactly, every time.
longForm.heroLead: Every variable in a slot-die coating run, head position, pump timing, substrate fixation, is a chance for the next run to drift from the last one. FOM alphaSC is built to close that gap. A protocol library saves your deposition process in full, so recalling it reproduces the same run with high precision and gives you real insight into which variables actually moved between attempts. A microporous substrate holder provides homogeneous suction across flexible or rigid substrates, removing the manual fixation steps that usually eat into setup time between samples. The slot-die head itself moves on automated vertical and lateral axes, run through software-integrated pump control, for a systematic, accelerated workflow rather than manual positioning guesswork. Add post-deposition units, drying, annealing, compressed gas for quick-drying, and docking modules, and the standalone tool grows into a small-scale pilot processing line, built to carry your research from lab-scale proof of concept toward a higher technology readiness level.

sections.glanceDescription: FOM alphaSC overview: automation, reproducibility, modular expansion, and application fit.
intro: FOM alphaSC overview: automated, reproducible slot-die coating for lab-scale thin-film research.

Reproducibility in slot-die coating usually comes down to whether every variable in the process, substrate fixation, head position, pump timing, stayed identical between runs. FOM alphaSC is designed around removing the manual steps that normally introduce that drift.

A microporous substrate holder applies homogeneous suction across the substrate surface, holding flexible or rigid materials in place without the taping, clipping, or manual fixturing that typically adds setup time before a run can even start. The slot-die head itself moves on automated vertical and lateral axes, coordinated with software-integrated pump control, turning what would otherwise be manual positioning into a repeatable, systematic process.

Everything a given run needs, positions, timing, pump settings, saves into a protocol library, so calling that protocol back reproduces the exact same deposition conditions later, with visibility into which variables actually differ if a result doesn't match.

paragraphs: Two things determine whether a coating run stays consistent from sample to sample: how the substrate is held, and how precisely the head is positioned over it. FOM alphaSC handles both automatically.

The microporous substrate holder applies suction evenly across the surface, which is what lets it hold both flexible and rigid substrates without the manual fixturing steps that would otherwise vary slightly between operators or runs. From there, the slot-die head's automated vertical and lateral movement, coordinated with software-integrated pump control, positions and runs the coating pass the same way every time, rather than depending on manual alignment.

Built around the same design goals as the rest of the FOM alpha family, eliminating experimental error and enhancing usability, it runs both flexible and rigid substrates on one platform, positioned for precision and reproducibility whether the work sits in early-stage academic research or production-scale industry use.
